lead_note: Final verdict = first-round verdict (Haiku medium GO, no rework). The judge verified the latest_bars key 'SPY|5 D|5 mins' is real (legacy.py:7427, 8063), so Haiku's first advisory was not a defect; the reference wired the provider via m5_chart_bars('SPY') instead.
notes: The behaviour matches the brief. tape_speed_light (technical_integrity.py diff lines 96-167) is generic, and tick_range_light (80-93) is a thin wrapper that keeps the TICK schema, the 'wide' label and the 1-decimal rounding. tape_light (203-240) falls back SPY, then TICK (wide becomes fast), then none with the SPY reason. The monitor writes market.tape fail-open in two try blocks (270-297) and leaves market.tick unchanged. All 4 hidden reference failures come from one cause: tape_light takes a pre-computed spy_light dict and has no as_of/spy_error keywords, while the reference takes bars plus as_of. The brief did not fix that signature, so this is an API mismatch, not a logic bug. The real gap is SESSION_HOUR_SPY_RANGE_NORMS (diff 58-66). It is clearly labelled as a stub from 4 local sessions, but its values run about 15-27% above the reference's 30-session norms in hours 0-4 (hour 1: 0.1058 vs 0.0834). The light would therefore read 'calm/normal' too often until it is re-derived; swapping in the 30-session values is the named fix. I checked the legacy.py wiring (diff 31-35): the 'SPY|5 D|5 mins' key is the real cache key (legacy.py:7427, 8063), it never touches IB, and the window filter keeps out the in-progress bar. The tests are thorough: thresholds, stale, completed-only, unreadable bars, fallback order, a raising provider and chip/tooltip. One small cosmetic point: the SPY tooltip drops the '%' unit. The self-review's GO is defensible and it flagged the 4-session stub, but it did not spell out the calibration effect. trading_risk: the light is display only, with no order or sizing path.
